patch_description: Builds on the beam-search framework but adds: (1) adaptive beam width — wide early (where pruning error compounds most), narrowing as partial schedules grow; (2) a wall-clock budget (~25s) so beam width and restarts scale to actual runtime rather than fixed counts; (3) diversified seeds per restart; and (4) a final insertion-move polish (relocate each transaction to its best position) applied to the best schedule found, which reliably shaves off remaining makespan that beam pruning leaves behind. The key insight from prior programs is that actual-cost evaluation at each step beats heuristics, and that greedy+local-search and beam search are complementary — beam explores broadly, polish exploits deeply.
